text:
Situation: Ifosfamide injection has been on the FDA shortage list since 2026-06-12 with updates through 2026-10-16. As of 2026-10-21 the shortage has been listed for 4 months. Corvale East holds 40 units at 7.3 per day for 6 days; Corvale Lakeside holds 28 units at 1.4 per day for 20 days; Corvale General holds 83 units at 5.8 per day for 14 days. Detailed stock shows East with 9 units of 50 mg/mL 60 mL (2.6 days) and 31 units of 1 g/20 mL (8.2 days); General with 41.12 and 42.29 units (14.4 days each); Lakeside with 19 units of 50 mg/mL 60 mL (26.5 days) and 9 units of 1 g/20 mL (13.8 days).

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the ifosfamide injection shortage on 2026-06-12 and updated it through 2026-10-16, listing Baxter Healthcare, Fresenius Kabi USA LLC, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc., and SteriMax Inc. as current.

Our position: East is critically low on the 50 mg/mL presentation. Lakeside and General have sufficient supply to support limited transfers without dropping below two weeks on hand.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 8 units of ifosfamide 50 mg/mL 60 mL from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East. Approval required: Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
2. Transfer 2 units of ifosfamide 1 g/20 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East. Approval required: Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
3. Use Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. ifosfamide 50 mg/mL as an alternate concentration or vial size. Recalculate dose and volume; pharmacist verification required. Approved by Riley Brooks, PharmD on 2026-09-15. Approval required: Pharmacist.
4. Use Baxter Healthcare Corporation ifosfamide 1 g/20 mL as an alternate concentration or vial size. Recalculate dose and volume; pharmacist verification required. Approved by Riley Brooks, PharmD on 2026-04-18. Approval required: Pharmacist.

Not recommended: No additional transfers or substitutions beyond those listed.
